name: compression-lab-category-portfolio-v1
result_policy: A category is won only after a frozen unseen-data pass against its strongest reproduced ratio baseline, its practical speed baseline, and every integrity, memory, portability, and accounting gate. Independent reproduction is required before a state-of-the-art claim.
completion_policy: Each category has ten equally weighted binary evidence gates. Partial, development-only, failed, stale, or merely planned evidence receives no credit for that gate. A category reaches 100% only after every gate is proven, including private holdout and independent reproduction. Percentages measure completion of the evidence program; they do not promise one codec setting can lead every conflicting speed and ratio metric.

completion_gate_definitions.requirement: Licensed development, lineage-disjoint public-validation, and external private-holdout policies are frozen before tuning.
The strongest credible practical and eligible specialist baselines are reproduced with complete artifact accounting.
A materially new candidate passes its complete predeclared development gate.
The frozen candidate passes every ratio, family, speed, memory, integrity, and accounting gate on previously unopened public validation.
The unchanged candidate passes its frozen external private holdout exactly once.
An independent party reproduces the category result from public instructions and evidence.
The candidate passes frozen compression and decompression speed tiers with stable repeated measurements.
Memory, streaming, and large-file gates pass with explicit bounds.
Exactness, determinism, corruption rejection, portability, and complete self-contained decoding pass.
The specialist is admitted behind bounded no-expansion selection, shipped in supported packages, and documented by a checksummed standardized comparison chart.

scorecard_required_fields: complete compressed bytes and byte-weighted ratio
compression and decompression MB/s with timing basis
peak memory or an explicit unmeasured marker
per-standard win, loss, mixed, or untested outcome

categories.label: JSON and machine-generated logs
categories.current_result: The immutable first CLUE-LDS public-validation score is a valid no-pass with a decisive ratio result: JLS2 produced 489,591 bytes from 96,934,483 source bytes, 52.97% smaller than the strongest eligible complete standard, Brotli-11 at 1,040,990 bytes. It won both previously unopened temporal families by 48.31% and 54.50%, compressed at 109.58 MB/s, and decoded at 431.36 MB/s. Every gate passed except standalone decoder memory: 651,517,952 bytes (621.3 MiB) exceeded the frozen 512 MiB cap. Both ranges are consumed and cannot be tuned or rerun. The result is public-validation ratio evidence, not a complete category win, private-holdout result, independent reproduction, or state-of-the-art claim.
tested_standards: official PBC-only on the frozen CLUE first score
categories.next_gate: Diagnose and reduce standalone decoder memory only on fresh licensed development families while preserving the imported no-pass unchanged. Do not tune or rerun on either consumed CLUE validation range. Require different untouched validation families, private-holdout success, and independent confirmation before a complete category or state-of-the-art claim.

categories.label: Multi-language source-code bundles
categories.specialist: open; adaptive-v3 remains a rejected legacy development path
categories.current_result: The frozen 15-codec practical development census completed all 630 trials exactly and deterministically. Kanzi-max was the ratio leader on all four source families and aggregated to 45,550,471 bytes from 529,449,573 source bytes (8.60%) at 3.47/2.95 MB/s compression/decompression and 1,890.5/1,909.7 MiB peak RSS. No Axiom candidate was entered, and the bounded research-ceiling tier remains pending, so this is baseline evidence rather than a category result.
categories.next_gate: Run the predeclared structural-transform probe and bounded research-ceiling tier, then route only a materially credible successor into the complete development gate.

categories.label: English Wikimedia revision text and wikitext
categories.specialist: open; the enwik9 corpus and published scores are diagnostic-only
categories.current_result: The frozen 15-codec practical development census completed all 630 trials exactly and deterministically. Kanzi-max led all three Wikimedia families and aggregated to 35,081,062 bytes from 201,311,173 source bytes (17.43%) at 2.37/2.30 MB/s compression/decompression and 1,529.5/1,525.8 MiB peak RSS. No Axiom candidate was entered; ZPAQ, paq8px, cmix, and NNCP remain pending in the bounded research-ceiling tier.
categories.next_gate: Run the predeclared structural-transform probe and bounded research-ceiling tier. Keep the enwik9 corpus and published scores outside every unseen gate; a shipped profile named enwik9 may appear only as a same-input baseline.

categories.label: Tabular CSV and delimited records
categories.current_result: On the frozen first public-validation score over four previously unseen CC-BY-4.0 UCI families, TBS1 beat the strongest exact per-family baseline by 7.35% to 16.50% on 3/4 families, but OCRB pixel tables were 32.15% larger and made aggregate output 3.48% larger than 7-Zip-9. Average speed, cold memory, exactness, determinism, fallback safety, portability, and complete accounting passed; one of five decompression repetitions missed the 250 MB/s floor. The overall gate did not pass.
categories.next_gate: Retain the failed first score and never tune or rerun on MetroPT, electricity, OULAD, or OCRB. Treat image-like pixel matrices as a separate category, develop any successor selector or representation only on fresh development families, and require a new untouched validation corpus.

categories.label: Numeric arrays and time-series data
categories.specialist: DMS2/DSS1 for byte-exact dense numeric matrices; time-series specialist remains open
categories.current_result: The retained first DMS2 public-validation score did not pass. On the two locked dense-matrix families, DMS2 was 46.57% larger than Brotli-11 on Gisette and 41.03% larger than bzip2-9 on Madelon; the two-item diagnostic aggregate was 43.55% larger than Brotli-11. Compression speed, minimum repetition speed, and cold compression memory also missed. Exactness, determinism, corruption rejection, decompression speed, bounded fallback, complete accounting, portability, and cross-platform wheels passed. A baseline manifest-scope defect independently invalidated the frozen aggregate corpus gate, and the complete deviation and first attempt are retained.
categories.next_gate: Do not tune or rerun DMS2 on Gisette or Madelon. Return dense matrices to fresh development research, fix corpus plumbing before any new lock, and require a materially new specialist to beat Brotli-11 and bzip2-9 on fresh development families before freezing different untouched validation families. Treat time-series, floating-point arrays, sparse arrays, and missing-value scientific data as separate wedges.

categories.label: General binary files and mixed archives
categories.current_result: No win against zstd-9; the current general encoder is not Pareto-optimal.
categories.next_gate: Retain safe direct/store fallback while category specialists mature; do not spend ratio research on a universal transform without a new measured hypothesis.

categories.label: Incompressible and already-compressed data
categories.current_result: The information-theoretically honest no-expansion, bounded-selector, adversarial-region, native-throughput, 1/4 GiB streaming, corruption, and second-platform gates are frozen. Existing fallback unit tests remain safety evidence only; the declared development corpus is not yet constructed and no category measurement exists.
categories.next_gate: Construct and byte-verify the five declared generated/licensed development families, then run the same-host 13-baseline census before changing the selector.
